thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> service=api-prod, symptom=HTTP 5xx rate spike, window=1m, threshold=5% (current=18%), alert_id=PD-89431 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-89431 created and paged the on-call rotation (routing key: prod-api). Escalation policy: auto-escalate after 120s if not acknowledged.

katie: acked. i'm on call, taking lead. starting quick triage — @mike can you pull the 5xx breakdown by route?

mike: pulling now, hitting grafana: /d/xyz/prod-api ->  /v1/generate shows most of the errors (502/503). looks like spike started ~ 1768001080 (~43s ago).

aj: seeing increased upstream latency to model-backend-3, connection resets in nginx logs. sample tail from nginx:```
2026/02/25 16:25:32 [error] 1234#0: *56789 recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.12.5.6, server: api-prod, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1"
```

katie: thanks. hypothesis: one model backend node started failing and nginx upstreams returned 502s. rolling routing fallback should already be configured but maybe not for long requests. check healthcheck and auto-fallback config.

davinder: looking at host metrics on model-backend-3 (host-3b). CPU fine, GPU memory OOMs around the same time in nvidia logs:```
E GPU OOM at 0x7f8a... memcpy failed
```
process crashed and restarted, container restarted 3x in last 2m. logs show new model load at 16:24:58 then oom.

mike: product traffic still high. 5xx rate 16% now. Most errors correlate to requests with sequence_length > 1024. seems we hit an unquantized model variant with large memory spike.

katie: mitigation plan: 1) temp route heavy/long requests to model-ops-fallback (lower-capacity variant but stable) 2) drop requests > 2048 tokens with 429 for a minute if fallback saturates 3) mark host-3b out of rotation.

aj: implementing host drain and marking host-3b unhealthy in service discovery. running:```
curl -X POST https://infra-api/hosts/host-3b/drain -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
ok host removed from upstream.

davinder: redeploy protection: I'm enabling model load cap so new containers won't try to load heavy model right now. patching config and rolling to the pool:```
service config set model_load_max_tokens=2048
```

mike: routing rule applied to split heavy requests -> model-ops-fallback. verifying: 200 routing hits to fallback in last 30s, fallback error rate 1%. overall 5xx dropped to 6%.

katie: nice. keep monitoring. @product-oncall any customer-impact notes we should surface?

product-oncall: a couple of enterprise customers reported degraded responses via support (timestamps match). impact: latency increased, some POSTs returned 502. Recommend proactive comms only if rate stays >10% for next 30m.

incident-bot: Auto-escalation timer paused (acknowledged by katie).

aj: ready for handoff in 25m. i'll continue watching host replacements and rollback protection.

katie: new numbers: overall 5xx at 3.2% now, /v1/generate 5xx at 4.5% but trending down. I'll keep the pager open for 45m for stability check.

mike: added short-lived alert suppression rule for noisy long requests to avoid repeated pages:```
alert.suppression.add(service='api-prod', rule='longreq-noise', duration=30m)
```

davinder: confirming model-backend-3 had corrupted checkpoint on disk — team will replace the node and reimage overnight. root cause: a model load path didn't validate checkpoint size and tried to allocate huge buffer for a bad file. filing follow-up: infra-1442.

product-oncall: noted action items: customer comms if >10% persist, follow-up postmortem, infra bug infra-1442, add model load validation + better OOM alerts.

katie: oncall handoff to aj at 17:05 UTC. aj you're set to page if anything regresses. closing initial mitigation; leaving ticket PD-89431 open for postmortem.

aj: acked handoff. will update PD and create a short incident summary once stabilized.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-89431 status -> acknowledged by katie. responders: katie, mike, aj, davinder.

katie: final note: we avoided customer-visible mass failures by graceful routing fallback and temporarily limiting model loads. good job team :thumbsup:
